# Fundamental Challenges in Evaluating Text2SQL Solutions and Detecting Their Limitations

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#evaluation-challenges)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.18197v1) · arXiv:2501.18197v1, 30 January 2025

**Reading coverage:** All 21 pages: sections 1–7, complete Appendix A.1–A.4 and all example rows, references, Tables 1–3; Figure 2 also visually inspected.

## Research question

Aggregate Text-to-SQL accuracy mixes model failures, incomplete or inaccurate benchmark inputs and labels, and biases in approximate SQL matching. These sources can require different remedies.

## Method

The paper organizes limitations into solution, evaluation-data, and evaluation-metric categories. It illustrates ambiguity from projection, filters, duplicate handling and schema information, then uses multiple LLM-generated query variants and disagreement to prioritize manual inspection.

## Evaluation

The evidence is an illustrative inspection of Spider examples and state-of-the-art systems, rather than a controlled comparison of a new detector. Appendix A lists 43 likely inaccurate-label examples and another 42 examples with other data issues.

## What the results support

A valid alternative interpretation may be penalized by a single reference, while match-function relaxations can accept incorrect predictions. The paper distinguishes genuine unanswerability and false presuppositions from ordinary generation failure and documents errors hidden by one database instance.

## Limits and qualifications

The example lists are explicitly incomplete, and model disagreement is a screening proxy rather than validated automatic error detection. Reported suspicious-example counts are not prevalence estimates for production data. Some examples depend on interpretation conventions; the taxonomy is not claimed complete.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Provides a useful vocabulary for designing ambiguity and abstention evaluation: state the allowed interpretations, available schema information and comparator behavior, and separate missing predictions from erroneous evaluation decisions.

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.
